items.q: What is the cheapest alternative to Systeme.io?
items.a: It depends on which part of Systeme.io's bundle you actually use, since Systeme.io itself starts free and its cheapest paid tier, Startup, already costs only $17 a month. A business that only needs email and light automation, with no funnel builder or course host, can run ActiveCampaign's entry plan for $15 a month billed annually, though that price covers only 1,000 contacts and a single user seat. A store with a real product catalog is usually cheaper on the free, self-hosted WooCommerce plugin, where the core software costs nothing and the bill becomes hosting instead of a subscription. Neither tool replaces the whole bundle: each swaps out only the one piece, email automation or ecommerce, that a specific business actually pays Systeme.io for today. Match the swap to the job you actually do, not to whichever number looks lowest on its own.

items.q: Is there a free alternative to Systeme.io?
items.a: Yes, though what counts as free depends on which piece of Systeme.io you rely on. Systeme.io's own Free plan already covers 2,000 contacts, three sales funnels and one course with a 0% transaction fee, so most searches for a free alternative are really asking about one specific limit on that plan. WooCommerce's core plugin is free with no contact or product cap at all, but it needs a self-hosted WordPress site, so hosting becomes the real bill even though the software itself costs nothing. Klaviyo's Free plan covers up to 250 active profiles and 500 email sends a month at no cost, useful for pure email and SMS rather than funnels or a course. Neither WooCommerce nor Klaviyo replaces Systeme.io's course tool or funnel builder for nothing; each is free only for the narrower job it actually does, so a course-first business is usually served better by Systeme.io's own Free plan than by stitching several free tools together.

items.q: What happens to my contacts and funnels if I cancel Systeme.io?
items.a: Contacts are the one piece Systeme.io actually helps you take with you: its help centre confirms you select your list from the Contacts screen, choose Export, and a CSV file is generated and emailed to your account address, downloadable for only 3 days before the link expires. Funnels, pages and course content have no matching export tool documented anywhere in Systeme.io's own help centre, so plan on rebuilding pages, email sequences and lessons by hand on whatever replaces it, not on migrating them automatically. Subscriptions are non-refundable under Systeme.io's terms, and a downgrade is not self-serve: you contact support, who send back a custom order form built around the lower plan's limits, while cancellation itself takes effect just before the next renewal date rather than immediately. Export your contact list, document your funnel steps and sequences, and confirm the new tool is live before that renewal date arrives.

items.q: Which Systeme.io alternative is best for a physical-product store?
items.a: Neither Systeme.io nor most funnel-building tools are really built for that job, since product variants are capped at 50 on Systeme.io's Free plan and rise only to 5,000 even on the $97 Unlimited plan. Shopify is the more direct answer: every plan allows unlimited products, and Shopify adds no transaction fee at all once a store uses Shopify Payments, starting at $39 a month for a single-owner store with no staff logins. WooCommerce is the free alternative for a business that already runs WordPress and wants to own its checkout and code instead of renting a hosted platform, though hosting, paid extensions and card processing then become separate bills managed on their own. Neither Shopify nor WooCommerce includes Systeme.io's course tool or its evergreen webinar funnels, so a store that also teaches or coaches would still need to add one of those separately.

items.q: Does any Systeme.io alternative include built-in SMS?
items.a: Yes, but priced and built differently from how Systeme.io handles it. Systeme.io has no messaging feature of its own: turning on SMS means connecting your own Twilio account and paying Twilio's rates directly, and its help centre states plainly that SMS costs and delivery are managed through Twilio. Klaviyo sells SMS as part of the same platform as its email tool, charging $0.01 per outbound US segment with carrier fees already included in that rate, so there is one bill instead of two accounts to manage. GoHighLevel goes further and bundles a full phone system, texting and calling included, into its $97-a-month Starter plan, though every text, call and phone number then bills separately on top of that plan from a prepaid usage wallet. Pick Klaviyo for email-and-SMS marketing with no CRM attached, and GoHighLevel when a phone system and a CRM matter as much as the messages themselves.

items.q: Is Kajabi a good alternative to Systeme.io?
items.a: For a course creator who has outgrown Systeme.io's caps, yes. Kajabi's entry-level Basic plan costs $179 a month, more than ten times Systeme.io's $17 Startup price, but in exchange it drops the fixed caps on funnels, landing pages and marketing emails that Systeme.io enforces on every tier below Unlimited. Kajabi also backs every plan with a 30-day money-back guarantee, something Systeme.io does not offer on any paid tier, since its subscriptions are non-refundable under its own terms. What Kajabi does not match is Systeme.io's price for a business just starting out: there is no free Kajabi plan, only a 14-day trial that requires a card upfront, against Systeme.io's Free plan, which needs no card and costs nothing indefinitely. Choose Kajabi once uncapped automation and a refund window matter more than the lowest possible bill; stay on Systeme.io while that is not yet true.

items.q: What's the closest alternative to Systeme.io for an agency managing several clients?
items.a: Systeme.io technically supports this through unlimited sub-accounts on every plan, but each sub-account only inherits its parent plan's own tags, funnels and automation-rule limits rather than getting a separate allowance, so an agency really needs the $97-a-month Unlimited plan before sub-accounts stop feeling cramped. GoHighLevel is built around this job specifically: its $97 Starter plan already includes 3 sub-accounts with their own CRM and phone system, and moving to the $297 Unlimited plan removes that cap and allows rebilling phone and email usage to clients at cost. GoHighLevel's own catch is usage: texts, calls and most AI still meter separately from a prepaid wallet, so the real bill runs above the plan price the moment clients start texting or calling through it. Pick GoHighLevel when clients need calling and texting under one roof; stick with a fully loaded Systeme.io Unlimited account when clients only need funnels, email and a course.
